generation.prompt:
Create ONE NEW original transparent LEVEL PLATFORM SPRITE for lesson four in the existing 星海远航 PBL learning website.
USER-CONFIRMED LESSON SUBJECT: pupils use SIMPLE EVERYDAY MATERIALS to BUILD REAL LIGHTWEIGHT AIRPLANE MODELS, then FLY THEM INSIDE THEIR CLASSROOM. This is a hands-on maker lesson, not computer operation, VR, simulator software, a full-size airplane or a professional factory.
Use the attached approved level-vr, level-theory and level-glider images as SAME-GROUP STYLE / PLATFORM references only. Create a DISTINCT new "模型制作与教室试飞" level. Do not duplicate the glider-experiment reference with its large completed airplane on launch rails.
MAIN TEACHING OBJECT on the rear half of the platform: one compact WOODEN MODEL-MAKING WORKBENCH with ivory/navy legs. On the tabletop, show a clearly recognizable SMALL LIGHTWEIGHT FOAM-BOARD / PAPER AND BALSA AIRPLANE being assembled: a slim simple wooden/cardboard fuselage, broad white foam/paper wings with sparse teal edge markings, simple small tail and amber tape joints. It should look classroom-made and lightweight, not a detailed RC aircraft or spacecraft. One wing panel can be beside the fuselage rather than fully attached, clearly communicating making and assembling. A small finished folded paper airplane rests beside it, showing a flyable outcome without making a second dominant aircraft.
SUPPORTING MATERIALS: one stack of cream paper/cardboard/foam sheets, one flat wing-shaped offcut, and a few LARGE readable craft tools such as a short ruler and rounded-tip scissors / amber tape roll. Keep only enough supporting objects to make the lesson recognizable; no tiny clutter. The model, separated wing and tools must be easily readable at 192-220 CSS pixels.
COMPOSITION: workbench and model are on the REAR HALF. Leave a CLEAR EMPTY FRONT-CENTER landing zone for the website's separate astronaut sprite, approximately x=50%,y=70% of the full image. Do not bake characters into the image. Maintain the same single floating octagonal engineering base, isometric 3/4 camera, upper-left light, ivory top tiles, dark navy mechanical underside, cyan edge lights, small amber rail posts, and short centered front steps as the references. Wood and paper provide warm classroom-maker character, while the base keeps the course's existing visual family. Entire silhouette inside square frame with genuinely transparent margins. No classroom scenery outside the platform.
ART DIRECTION: original coarse retro 16-bit pixel clusters, clean staircase contours, navy outlines, ivory structures, cyan highlights, warm wood and restrained gold. 2-3 flat shading bands per material, bold 64-96 logical-pixel feel; consistent visible pixel scale and clear object silhouette, not a smooth illustration with grain. No 3D render, continuous gradients, soft glow, antialiasing, photorealism, paint texture, dithering, blur, noise or microscopic detail.
OUTPUT: ONE square 1024x1024 asset with true transparent alpha outside platform. No words, letters, numbers, watermark, school crest, route, labels, question mark, lock, badge, avatar, astronaut, person, UI or background/checkerboard. No computer monitors, control consoles, VR headsets or launch rails. The scene must clearly communicate children MAKING simple model airplanes for indoor trial flights, while keeping the same art family as the three references.
